name: Jacksonville Beach
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Jacksonville Beach, FL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas at the Beaches: Deck the Chairs, Beaches North Pole Express, Beaches Town Center tree lighting and Neptune Beach's golf cart parade.
lede: Jacksonville Beach does Christmas on the sand and at the Beaches Museum, with decorated lifeguard chairs, a museum North Pole Express and a tree lighting shared with Atlantic Beach and Neptune Beach.
celebrates: Jacksonville Beach celebrates Christmas beside the ocean. Deck the Chairs turns Latham Plaza and the Seawalk Pavilion into a walk past decorated lifeguard chairs, with lights, live entertainment and student art, and a Christmas market on five Sundays. Beaches Museum runs the Beaches North Pole Express, with Santa, cocoa and a trackless train, then Christmas at the Cabin with chapel performances and a marshmallow fire. Next door, Atlantic Beach and Neptune Beach share the Beaches Town Center tree lighting, and Neptune Beach adds Christmas in the Park and a golf cart and bike parade.
lastyear: In 2025 Beaches Museum held the Beaches North Pole Express on Friday, December 12, from 3 to 6 pm, and Saturday, December 13, from 10 am to 2 pm. Families met Santa and the North Pole Express Conductor, shared cocoa and cookies, rode a trackless train, saw train displays and made holiday crafts, with free registration. The Beaches Town Center Holiday Celebration and Tree Lighting ran Saturday, December 6, 2025, from 3 to 7 pm at Beaches Town Center, according to the City of Atlantic Beach calendar.
facts: Jacksonville Beach began because of a railroad. Beaches Museum says that in 1884 William and Eleanor Scull set up their tent home at the beach to help survey the area for the coming railroad. Visit Jacksonville says the town was renamed Pablo Beach on May 13, 1886, and the name changed to Jacksonville Beach on June 15, 1925. Beaches Museum sits at 381 Beach Boulevard and keeps a History Park, a chapel and a depot on its grounds, which is where the holiday train events happen.
trains: Jacksonville Beach has a real Christmas train story at Beaches Museum. The museum's own operating North Pole Express arrives at its Mayport Depot for the holiday season, and an earlier museum page says it temporarily replaces the Florida East Coast Railroad train normally displayed in the Upper Depot. During the Beaches North Pole Express days, children also ride a trackless train in the History Park. For a bigger rail history stop, Jacksonville's 1919 terminal is now the Prime F. Osborn III Convention Center.

kidfact: Jacksonville Beach used to be called Pablo Beach. The name changed to Jacksonville Beach on June 15, 1925, almost forty years after the town was renamed Pablo Beach in 1886.
faq: What is Deck the Chairs in Jacksonville Beach?

Deck the Chairs is a holiday tradition at Latham Plaza and the Seawalk Pavilion in Jacksonville Beach. Its own site describes decorated lifeguard chairs, lights, live entertainment and student art. Visit Jacksonville lists it from November 25 into January, and the organizers say admission to stroll the chairs is free.
Can kids ride a train at Christmas in Jacksonville Beach?

Beaches Museum offers a trackless train ride during the Beaches North Pole Express on December 11 and 12, 2026, and the museum's North Pole Express train is on display at the Mayport Depot for the season. The event is free for children, with $5 for non-member adults, and registration is required.
When is the tree lighting at the Beaches?

The Holiday Celebration and Tree Lighting is Saturday, December 5, 2026, from 3 to 7 pm at Beaches Town Center, where Atlantic Boulevard meets the ocean. The Beaches Town Center Agency calls it free, with hayrides, craft tables, performers and Santa. Neptune Beach also lights its own tree at Christmas in the Park on December 4.
Is there a Christmas parade near Jacksonville Beach?

Neptune Beach holds the 1st Street Christmas Golf Cart and Bike Parade on Saturday, December 5, 2026. Lineup is at 2 pm and the parade begins at 3 pm, ending at Beaches Town Center in time for the tree lighting. Families can decorate a golf cart or bike to join.
Are Atlantic Beach and Neptune Beach events on this page?

Yes. Atlantic Beach and Neptune Beach have too few verified kids' events for their own pages, so the Beaches Town Center tree lighting, Neptune Beach's Christmas in the Park and its golf cart parade are listed here with Jacksonville Beach, as the three towns share the same stretch of coast.
intro_html:

We check every date on the host's own website, and each listing links straight there.
